classes.finest_note: Polling table (mesa) in ONPE's open data from 2006 (district totals for 2000 and 2001); Infogob carries national totals only
classes.locator: https://www3.congreso.gob.pe/Docs/constitucion/constitucion/Constitucion-web_2026.pdf (arts. 111-112: direct election, absolute majority of valid votes, runoff of the top two within 30 days, five-year term)
classes.note: A ticket of the president and two vice presidents in one national constituency that includes voters abroad. Under the 1933 Constitution a candidate needed a third of the valid votes, failing which Congress chose; the 1979 Constitution set a 36% rule for 1980 only and an absolute majority from 1985, kept by the 1993 Constitution (art. 111). Infogob's record starts in 1931; the direct and indirect presidential elections of the nineteenth century and of 1919-1929 are not in any official machine-readable series and are not itemized here.

classes.note: 120 members until 2011 and 130 from 2011, by D'Hondt (cifra repartidora) with optional double preference votes (LOE arts. 21, 30). A single national constituency in 1995 and 2000; 25 constituencies from 2001, 26 from 2011 with Lima Provincias, and 27 from 2021 with Peruvians abroad. The 2020 election followed the dissolution of Congress by Decreto Supremo 165-2019-PCM and filled the rest of the 2016-2021 term. Ley 31988 replaced the body with a Senate and a Chamber of Deputies from the 2026 general election.

classes.name: Senado de la República
classes.locator: https://portal.jne.gob.pe/portal_documentos/files/e37c4208-5113-4609-8959-9b46e12d2e40.pdf (art. 21: at least 60 senators for five years, 30 by majority in 27 constituencies (four by proportional representation in Lima Metropolitana) and the rest by proportional representation in one national constituency)
classes.note: Three eras. Under the 1933 Constitution senators were elected by department with votes for candidates (1936 annulled, 1939, 1945, 1950, 1956, 1962 annulled, 1963), with supplementary elections in 1946 and 1951 where the vote had been annulled. Under the 1979 Constitution 60 senators were elected in one national constituency (1980, 1985, 1990) until the 1992 self-coup dissolved Congress. Ley 31988 restored the Senate from 2026: 30 seats by constituency and 30 by national list, with a 5% threshold of valid votes and of seats (LOE art. 20). Before 1931 Congress was elected under earlier constitutions not covered by Infogob.

classes.locator: https://portal.jne.gob.pe/portal_documentos/files/e37c4208-5113-4609-8959-9b46e12d2e40.pdf (art. 21: at least 130 deputies for five years by proportional representation in 27 constituencies, two for Peruvians abroad)
classes.note: Under the 1933 Constitution deputies were elected by department or province with votes for candidates (1936 annulled, 1939, 1945, 1950, 1956, 1962 annulled, 1963), with supplementary elections in 1946 and 1951. Restored by Ley 31988 from 2026 with 130 seats in 27 constituencies, a 5% threshold of valid votes and of seats (LOE art. 20), and the JNE's seat apportionment (Resolución 0053-2025-JNE).

classes.note: Each authority named in a petition is a separate question, voted in the municipality or region; an authority is removed by half plus one of the valid votes with at least half of the electorate voting (Ley 26300 art. 23, as amended). Since Ley 30315 (2015) consultations are held once per term, in its third year. Held in provincial and district municipalities; no regional authority has gone to a vote. Lima Metropolitana's 2013 consultation is the largest. Infogob counts the municipalities (circunscripciones) voting: 61 in 1997, 173 in 2001, 188 in 2004, 15 and 6 in 2005, 245 in 2008, 72 in 2009, 270 in 2012, 3 and 124 in 2013, 27 in 2017, 13 in 2021, and 4 in 2025.

classes.note: A governor and vice governor on one ticket in each of the 25 regions (the 24 departments, with Lima's region covering only Lima Provincias, and the Callao); the Municipality of Lima Metropolitana exercises regional powers and elects no governor. Elected by plurality in 2002 and 2006; since 2010 a ticket needs 30% of the valid votes, otherwise the top two meet in a second round (Ley 27683 art. 5 as amended by Ley 29470). classes.name: Elecciones primarias y elecciones internas organizadas por la ONPE

classes.finest_note: Polling table (mesa) in ONPE's open data
classes.locator: https://leyes.congreso.gob.pe/Documentos/Leyes/28094.pdf (arts. 19-24 as amended by Leyes 30998 and 32058: primaries organized by ONPE, by members or by delegates)
classes.note: ONPE runs the candidate selection of every party and regional movement on fixed days, by vote of members or of delegates the members elect. The 2021 general election used party internal elections organized by ONPE on 29 November and 6 December 2020 (president, Congress, Andean Parliament, and delegates); the 2022 regional and municipal elections on 15 and 22 May 2022; complementary municipal elections in 2023, 2024, and 2025. The 2026 general election used primaries on 30 November 2025 (members) and 7 December 2025 (delegates), and the 2026 regional and municipal elections on 17 and 24 May 2026. Parties that fail the primaries' participation threshold cannot field candidates.

classes.note: Justices of the peace are chosen by the residents of their jurisdiction for four years, in a vote the superior court of justice calls and the community organizes, or by the court from a list when no vote is held (Ley 29824 arts. 7-9; LOE art. 24). classes.name: Elección del Presidente por el Congreso (Constitución de 1933)
classes.name_en: President chosen by Congress when no candidate won a third
classes.locator: https://infogob.jne.gob.pe/Localidad (ELECCIONES GENERALES 1962 - PRESIDENCIAL: LAS ELECCIONES FUERON ANULADAS)
classes.note: Under the 1933 Constitution, when no candidate won a third of the valid votes Congress chose among the leading three. The 1962 election was such a case, but the military annulled it before Congress voted.
classes.disposition_reason: A vote of members of Congress, not of the public, and never completed.

classes.note: Presidents of the chambers, regional and municipal officers chosen by their councils, the National Board of Justice, and the JNE's plenary are chosen by members of public bodies or by competition.
